title: Claude Buried Your Answer In A Wall Of Text — One Line Fixes It 🧱
tags: claude artifacts,claude ai tips,wall of text,ai productivity,claude tips,artifact panel,ai for beginners,prompt tips,claude ai,ai writing,ai tips
_demo_note: IN-HOUSE MOCK, not a vendor tape. The planned path was a real logged-in claude.ai capture (record_demo.py --site claude --require-login --redact-pii --followup). Plan-time preflight passed (logged_in:true, 'Artifacts' visible), but the live take failed on TWO independent gates, so the brief's sanctioned fallback was taken: (1) the prompt was never actually submitted - Enter did not send on claude.ai's tiptap composer, the URL stayed on /new and the text sat in the composer, so watch_answer never saw an answer and first_token came back None (this is exactly the SITES/ANSWER_SELECTORS gap the file's own playbook 10b comment warns about: ANSWER_SELECTORS carries only chatgpt/desktop markup and matches NOTHING on claude.ai); (2) the 540x960 mobile viewport renders the recents sidebar EXPANDED, and its body text carried real personal conversation titles and the account name - redaction could not be verified clean frame-by-frame. The 84s take was DELETED rather than shipped or held. Demo beats are therefore scripts/make_artifact_mock.py (playbook 13 grammar: no vendor name, no logo, no lookalike branding, ILLUSTRATIVE footer inside the caption-safe band). The Artifacts concept is generic and the fact is uncontested, so a labelled mock is honest here - but this episode shows OUR mock, and the script never claims to be showing the product.

_beat_note: PROOF-AT-4s, achieved STRUCTURALLY not by clipping words. Two earlier cuts failed the 4.0s gate at 4.81s and 4.82s: three pre-panel lines carry 3x0.4s of locked breaks, leaving ~2.8s of speech for the hook + wall + fix, i.e. ~6 words total - unshippable against the brief's own 'comprehension pacing, NOT max speed' rule. Clipping line 3 to 'One line.' gained NOTHING (4.81 -> 4.82s) because ElevenLabs re-draws the whole take and lines 1-2 grew to absorb the saving; TTS duration is not deterministic, so chasing the gate word-by-word is unbounded. The fix: mock_ask.png ALREADY shows the wall of text AND the typed 'put that in an artifact' in the composer, so the separate hold_wall beat was redundant. Dropping it removes one line and one 0.4s break from the pre-panel run: wall+fix both land at 2.07s and the ARTIFACT PANEL renders at 3.82s, under the gate with real margin. hold_wall.mp4 is retained on disk, now unused. SINGLE-BEAT: one move, no stacked demos.
_steps_note: Three chips over the three teaching beats (type the line -> panel renders -> copy it), re-probed with probe_frames.py corner over the NEW cut windows (Ep26 rule). Ep25 v4 rule - reading what the ink IS: tl carries only the decorative 'AI ASSISTANT' header strip, which sits above the artifact panel's top edge and above the wall body, so a tl chip never covers the content being taught. br is rejected on the ask beat despite scoring clean: it sits on the composer, which is the thing that beat is teaching.
